chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no objection to buying green crops; if you wish, you may leave them until you harvest them, and if you wish, sell them as grass."
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying and selling green crops before harvest?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on *bay' al-qiraad* (sale of standing green crops), affirming its validity by granting the buyer discretion to either hold the crop until harvest or sell it in its pre-harvest, grassy state. This flexibility underscores the permissibility of trading agricultural produce before it is fully separated from the earth, a key distinction in Shia commercial jurisprudence that prevents uncertainty (*gharar*) regarding the existence and quality of the goods.
